extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI). The user-controlled 'name' query parameter (bound at line 19) is interpolated into an f-string at line 38 and then compiled/evaluated as a Jinja2 template by Template(content).render() at line 41. Jinja2's Template() uses an environment with autoescape disabled by default, so attacker input such as ?name={{7*7}} is evaluated server-side. This escalates to remote code execution via Python object introspection (e.g. {{''.__class__.__mro__[2].__subclasses__()}} to reach subprocess.Popen).

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine (Server-Side Template Injection)

extra.message: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). The 'name' query parameter is concatenated directly into an HTML f-string at line 38 without output encoding, and the resulting string is rendered by Jinja2's Template(content).render() at line 41 where autoescaping is disabled for string templates. A payload such as ?name=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> is emitted as raw HTML to the browser. The externally fetched 'public_ip' value (line 36) is likewise injected unescaped, providing a second XSS source.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Hardcoded credential. SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN is set to the literal '5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n' instead of being read from an environment variable, as explicitly acknowledged by the '# FIXME: os.getenv("SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN")' comment. The secret is committed to source control and identical across every deployment, so anyone with repository or image access obtains the token.

Hardcoded secret. SUPER_SECRET_NAME is set to the literal 'John Ripper' instead of being read from an environment variable, as indicated by the '# FIXME: os.getenv("SUPER_SECRET_NAME")' comment. The value is committed to source control and used as the default for the 'name' parameter (app/main.py:19), making it identical across all deployments.

Active debug code / security misconfiguration. FastAPI is instantiated with debug=config.DEBUG (line 14), where config.DEBUG is derived from the DEBUG environment variable (app/config.py:9) and the committed .env_temp sets DEBUG=True. When enabled, FastAPI returns verbose HTML error pages containing stack traces, local file paths, variable values, and source snippets to unauthenticated clients, leaking internal implementation details.
